lessons.title: The new kickoff
lessons.objective: You can explain the dynamic kickoff in one sentence.

payload.prompt: Where does the receiving team start after a kickoff touchback?

diagram.alt: Football field showing the receiving team's 35-yard line, where the ball is placed after a kickoff touchback.

explanation.correct: Since 2025, a kickoff touchback comes out to the 35-yard line. The dynamic kickoff arrived in 2024, and the league moved the touchback spot up to encourage returns.
explanation.incorrect: The 40-yard line is where the kicking team lines up, not where a touchback is spotted. A touchback is placed at the 35.
explanation.sayThisLine: A touchback on a kickoff comes out to the 35.

payload.prompt: Why did the NFL change the kickoff in 2024?

options.text: To keep returns in the game while cutting high-speed collisions
To make the kicker more valuable
To speed up the game

explanation.correct: Kickoffs had a high injury rate. The dynamic kickoff starts most players close together and limits running starts, so the play stays exciting with fewer big collisions.
explanation.incorrect: The change was about player safety and keeping the return alive. The kicking team lines up at the receiving team's 40, which shortens the running start.

payload.prompt: Returner catches the ball at the 38-yard line and is tackled at the 45.

scene.alt: A football play showing a kickoff return from the 38 to the 45-yard line.

explanation.correct: The returner caught it in the field and advanced it. That is a 7-yard gain. A touchback only happens if the ball lands in the end zone or goes out of bounds.
explanation.incorrect: A touchback is when the ball enters the end zone. This returner caught it at the 38 and ran it to the 45, so it is a 7-yard return.

payload.prompt: Match the kickoff outcome to where the ball ended up.

pairs.definition: The returner catches the kick and advances it before being tackled.
A kick that reaches the end zone and is downed there; the receiving team starts at the 35 (since 2025).
The kicking team's ten coverage players start on the receiving team's 40; the kicker stays back.

explanation.summary: A return is when the ball is fielded and advanced. A touchback ends the play in the end zone. The kickoff setup is where the kicking team starts.
explanation.sayThisLine: He brought it back out of the end zone, so no touchback.

lessons.title: Fair catch and returns
lessons.objective: You can say when a fair catch is smart.

payload.prompt: Returner waves his arm at the kick, then catches it and runs.

scene.alt: A football play showing a returner waving and then attempting to run with the kickoff.

choices.label: Fair catch, the play ends at the catch

explanation.correct: Once he signals for a fair catch, he cannot run it back. The play ends where he catches it, and he gets protection from hits. He chose safety over yards.
explanation.incorrect: A fair catch signal means he cannot advance. Waving commits him to catching it in place.

payload.prompt: Punt falling at your 12, coverage closing. Fair catch or return?

situation.narrative: Your team leads by three with two minutes left. The punt is coming down near your 12-yard line with the coverage team arriving fast.

options.label: Signal fair catch
options.consequence: You secure the ball and avoid a hit. Your offense takes over and can run the clock.
considerations: You are ahead and protecting the lead

options.label: Catch it and try to return it
options.consequence: With tacklers on top of you, a few yards is the best case and a fumble would hand them a short field.

payload.expertNote: Fair catch is about field position and risk. When you lead and the coverage is on top of you, securing the ball is usually worth more than a few extra yards.

payload.prompt: After a fair catch, where does the next play start?

options.text: At the spot of the catch
At the returner's own 20-yard line
At midfield

explanation.correct: The play ends where the returner catches the ball, and the offense starts from that spot. That is what he gives up for the safety of a fair catch: no return yards.
explanation.incorrect: A fair catch is marked at the spot of the catch. There is no automatic move to the 20 or midfield.
explanation.sayThisLine: Fair catch, so they start right where he caught it.

payload.prompt: Match the return scenario to the result.

pairs.definition: The returner waves his arm and the play ends where he catches it.
A kick that reaches the end zone and is downed; the receiving team starts at the 35 (since 2025).
The area from the goal line to the 20-yard line where a dynamic kickoff is meant to land.

explanation.summary: Fair catch stops the play where caught. A kickoff that reaches the end zone comes out to the 35, and the landing zone is where the kick is meant to come down.
explanation.sayThisLine: He fair-caught it, so the play is dead right there.

lessons.title: Punting
lessons.objective: You can say why a punt is a weapon, not a surrender.

payload.prompt: What is the best reason to punt on fourth down?

options.text: You are giving up because you do not trust your offense
You are moving the opponent back, improving your field position
The rules require you to punt on fourth down

explanation.correct: A punt trades a possession for field position: the opponent now starts farther from your end zone. A 40-yard net punt pushes them 40 yards away.
explanation.incorrect: A punt is not surrender, it is field-position math. On fourth down deep in your own territory, pushing the opponent back is often the smartest choice.

payload.prompt: A punt travels 50 yards and the returner brings it back 5. What is the net?

explanation.correct: Fifty yards minus five yards of return is a 45-yard net. Net punting shows how much field position the kick actually gained.
explanation.incorrect: Net distance is the kick's length minus the return: 50 minus 5 is 45 yards.

payload.prompt: Punter aims for the opponent's sideline at their 5-yard line.

scene.alt: A football field showing a punt aimed at the opponent's sideline near the goal line.

explanation.correct: A coffin-corner punt lands out of bounds near the goal line, pinning the opponent deep in their own territory. It is a great kick and hard to execute.
explanation.incorrect: A coffin corner is a punt that goes out of bounds near the opponent's goal line, giving them poor field position. A touchback is only if the ball lands in the end zone.

payload.prompt: Match the punt outcome to the result.

pairs.definition: The ball travels far downfield; great field position for the defense.
Punt out of bounds near the goal line, pinning the opponent deep.
The ball enters the end zone, and the receiving team takes over at the 20-yard line.

explanation.summary: Long punts are powerful weapons. Coffin corners are precision kicks. Touchbacks give the opponent decent field position.
explanation.sayThisLine: That coffin-corner punt pinned them at the five.

lessons.title: Field goals
lessons.objective: You can guess whether a kick is in range.

payload.prompt: Your offense is at the opponent's 30-yard line. How long is the field goal attempt?

explanation.correct: Add about 17 yards to the yard line: 10 for the end zone and about 7 for the snap and hold. 30 plus 17 is a 47-yard attempt.
explanation.incorrect: Field-goal range is roughly the yard line plus 17 yards. From the 30, that is about 47 yards, a long kick but within range for many NFL kickers.

payload.prompt: Offense at the opponent's 25-yard line on fourth and four.

scene.alt: Football scenario showing fourth down decision at the opponent's 40-yard line.

explanation.correct: From the 25, it is a 42-yard attempt, which NFL kickers usually make. Going for it is a fair debate in some games, but taking three points is a solid choice.
explanation.incorrect: A field goal from the 25 is a 42-yard kick, close to automatic for most NFL kickers. Going for it risks giving the ball back with nothing.

payload.prompt: After a touchdown, how far is the extra-point kick?

options.text: 20 yards from the goal line
33 yards (snapped from the 15-yard line)
It varies based on the touchdown location

explanation.correct: The extra-point kick is snapped from the 15-yard line, making it roughly a 33-yard attempt. Most kickers make 95 percent of these. It is a chip shot.
explanation.incorrect: The extra-point attempt is snapped from the 15, which is 33 yards out (including snap depth and holder distance). It is almost automatic.

payload.prompt: Down 6, 30 seconds left, at the opponent's 50. Kick?

situation.narrative: You are down 6 with 30 seconds left. Your offense just reached the opponent's 50-yard line.

options.label: Attempt the 67-yard field goal
options.consequence: Even a made kick would only cut the lead to three, and 67 yards is beyond almost every kicker. The game ends.
considerations: You cannot get the ball back

options.label: Go for the touchdown
options.consequence: You need six points and have time for a few plays. It is a long shot, but it is the only way to win.
considerations: A field goal is not enough
Your kicker cannot make this kick

payload.expertNote: Down six, only a touchdown wins, so a field goal does not help even for a great kicker. The decision here is about the score, not just the kicker.

lessons.title: The onside kick
lessons.objective: You can explain the onside kick and the 2026 change.

payload.prompt: What is an onside kick?

options.text: A short kick the kicking team tries to recover for a second possession
A kick that stays in bounds for the entire flight
A penalty for kicking out of bounds

explanation.correct: An onside kick is a short kick, usually about 10 to 15 yards, that the kicking team tries to recover. It must travel at least 10 yards before the kicking team can touch it.
explanation.incorrect: An onside kick is intentionally short so the kicking team can try to recover it. It is a desperation play when you need the ball back quickly.

statement.speaker: Announcer
statement.text: New for 2026: a team can declare an onside kick any time, not just late in the game.

payload.question: What changed from before?

options.text: Teams no longer have to wait until late in the game to declare an onside kick
The receiving team must stand still during an onside kick
Onside kicks must travel exactly 10 yards
The kicking team gets two onside kicks per game

payload.translation: The kicking team can now declare an onside kick at any point, and the receiving team must put five players on the restraining line. Onside kicks stay a low-percentage bet.

followUps.line: When would you want an onside kick?
followUps.why: Tests whether you understand field situations where recovering the ball matters more than field position.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Onside kicks are rare and risky. Ask yourself whether the team needs the ball back more than it fears giving up field position.

payload.prompt: Onside kick goes 12 yards, then a kicking-team player recovers it.

scene.alt: Football play showing an onside kick recovery with both teams converging on the ball.

explanation.correct: The ball travelled at least 10 yards, so the kicking team may legally recover it and keep the ball. That is the whole point of an onside kick.
explanation.incorrect: A kicking-team recovery counts once the ball has gone 10 yards. If it had gone less, the receiving team would get the ball.

payload.prompt: Match the kick type to when it is used.

pairs.definition: A short kick the kicking team tries to recover, used when desperately needing the ball back.
A deep kick to the landing zone with the coverage team at the receiving team's 40. Starts a half or follows a score.
A punt aimed out of bounds near the goal line to pin the opponent deep.

explanation.summary: Onside is short and desperate. The deep kickoff is the norm. Coffin corners are punts.
explanation.sayThisLine: That was an onside kick, they are trying to recover it.

lessons.title: Special teams talk
lessons.objective: You can hear a special teams complaint and translate it.

statement.speaker: Coach
statement.text: Our hang time stinks. The returner had too much time.

payload.question: What is he upset about?

options.text: The kicker did not give the special teams coverage time to get downfield
The returner took too long to decide
The game is too long
The team waited too long to call timeout

payload.translation: Hang time is how long the ball stays in the air. A short one means the coverage team arrives late, so the returner has more room. The kicker should kick higher.

followUps.line: How do you improve hang time?
followUps.why: Tests whether you know it is a kicking technique, not a coverage issue alone.

payload.noFakeExpertNote: Special teams is underrated. Ask: Did the kick give us time or did the return look easy?

payload.title: Special teams moment
payload.setting: Your friend texts you about a terrible return on a big third-quarter kickoff.

exchanges.theirMessage: Did you see that kickoff return? Our guy fumbled at the 30 and they recovered. Brutal.

replies.text: Ouch, a fumble there hands them a short field. Has he been shaky all year?
replies.theirResponse: Honestly, no. It was his first fumble all season.
replies.coachNote: You named why it hurts and asked a real question.

replies.text: That returner is terrible. You should bench him.
replies.theirResponse: I mean, one mistake. He usually brings them back.
replies.coachNote: Overreacting to one play loses you trust. Every player has a bad moment.

replies.text: That is what you get with the new kickoff.
replies.theirResponse: Not really. That one was about ball security.
replies.coachNote: The kickoff rule did not cause a fumble, and it missed her point about field position. Listen first.

exchanges.theirMessage: Yeah. They kicked a field goal off it. We were up by three and now it is tied.

replies.text: That fumble changed the whole drive. Is he the backup returner or the starter?
replies.theirResponse: He is the starter. Not sure what happened to him today.
replies.coachNote: You asked a genuine question that invited her to talk more, instead of just agreeing.

replies.text: Yeah, special teams lost this game.
replies.theirResponse: It is the third quarter. Long way to go.
replies.coachNote: The game is far from over. Do not write off the whole game yet.

replies.text: We should stop using that guy on returns.
replies.theirResponse: Let's not overreact over one play.
replies.coachNote: A fix is fine, but listening to her take first builds trust.

payload.closingNote: Special teams decide close games. One fumble or a great return flips momentum.

payload.prompt: What is special teams?

options.text: The offense and defense when they are performing well
Kickoffs, punts, field goals and returns: the third phase of the game
Only the players who are exceptional athletes

explanation.correct: Special teams is the third phase: kickoffs, punts, field goals, PATs and returns. It decides more games than people realize, especially close ones.
explanation.incorrect: Special teams is a whole phase of the game with its own coaches, players and schemes. It includes kickers, punters, long snappers and returners.

payload.prompt: Punt comes down high at midfield. Fair catch or field return?

situation.narrative: Your team is down 7 with four minutes left. The punt hangs up for almost four seconds.

facts.label: Coverage
facts.value: Gunners arriving as the ball lands

options.label: Fair catch
options.consequence: You start at midfield with four minutes and no fumble risk. That is plenty of time to score.
considerations: Midfield is a solid starting spot

options.label: Field return
options.consequence: The coverage is closing, so the upside is a few yards and the downside is a fumble that ends your comeback.
considerations: A return could gain a little field position

payload.expertNote: A long hang time gives the coverage time to arrive, so a clean fair catch at midfield is usually worth more than a few extra yards. A returner with open space can go.
